title: Regression formulas omit the nondegenerate-design and sample-size prerequisites

evidence.detail: b1 and ck divide by A=sum (Xk-Xbar)^2, yet no A>0 assumption is stated.
residual variance uses chi-square(n-2) and divides by n-2 without requiring n>2.
the appendix repeats the b1 formula without the nonconstant-X condition.

why: If all predictors are equal, A=0 and neither slope nor the displayed coefficients exist. If n<=2, the residual-variance statistic has nonpositive degrees of freedom. Both cases are admitted by the present statement.
suggested_correction: State A>0 (at least two distinct predictor values) before the OLS formulas; require n>2 for residual variance/t inference, and state the normal independent-error assumptions where exact distributional claims are made.

title: CLT standardization permits zero variance even though its denominator is then zero

evidence.detail: The theorem assumes only Var[X1]=sigma^2<infinity, then divides by sigma.
The reference-sheet CLT repeats the same condition and denominator.

why: For a constant iid sequence sigma=0, so (S_n-nmu)/(sigma sqrt(n)) is undefined and cannot converge to N(0,1).
suggested_correction: Require 0<sigma^2<infinity; treat the zero-variance case separately as a degenerate constant sum.

title: Binomial and Poisson mode statements lose the integer-parameter tie case

evidence.detail: States a unique binomial mode floor(p(n+1)) and Poisson mode floor(lambda).

why: If p(n+1) is an integer m with 0<p<1, Bin(n,p) has modes m-1 and m; if lambda is a positive integer m, Poi(lambda) has modes m-1 and m. Example: Bin(1,1/2) has both 0 and 1, whereas the displayed rule returns only 1.
suggested_correction: Add the tie cases; otherwise retain floor(p(n+1)) and floor(lambda) when the respective quantity is nonintegral.

title: One-dimensional density-change formula is stated under insufficient regularity

evidence.detail: The theorem assumes only strict monotonicity but uses a differentiable inverse in its conclusion.
The sheet shortens this further to merely 'monotone g'.

why: Monotonicity alone neither guarantees an inverse derivative nor that the pushforward remains absolutely continuous. The displayed formula needs an invertible differentiable/absolutely-continuous transformation with the usual nonzero-derivative qualification (at least almost everywhere on the relevant support).
suggested_correction: State the regularity explicitly, e.g. g is one-to-one and differentiable on the support with differentiable inverse (or use the a.e. absolutely-continuous version), and give the support of Y.

title: Formula-sheet confidence and variance procedures suppress their exact sampling hypotheses

evidence.detail: The mean CIs and chi-square variance pivot are presented without stating iid normal observations, n>=2, and the appropriate known/unknown-mean case.
The source example explicitly begins with n independent identically distributed normal observations and known sigma for the first interval.
The chi-square pivot is explicitly tied to X~N(mu,sigma^2) with known mu.

why: The t and chi-square equalities are not distribution-free. The compressed sheet could lead a reader to use exact tables for nonnormal/dependent data or the wrong degrees-of-freedom pivot.
suggested_correction: Prefix the statistics block with 'for an iid normal sample'; distinguish the known-mu variance pivot (df n) from the unknown-mu pivot (df n-1), and list n constraints.

title: Continuous-distribution table lacks the parameter and MGF-domain conditions needed to use it safely

evidence.detail: Rows omit a<b, lambda>0, alpha>0, beta>0, sigma>0, and n>0; Gamma's MGF row also omits t<beta and uniform's displayed quotient is undefined at t=0.
The lecture does explicitly require lambda>0 for Exponential, demonstrating the lost condition.

why: Without these restrictions several expressions are not densities or are undefined. The MGF conditions matter because a formula valid near zero is required for moment generation.
suggested_correction: Add a compact conditions note under the table: a<b; lambda,alpha,beta,sigma>0; n in positive integers; Gamma MGF t<beta; and interpret the uniform MGF at t=0 by continuity as 1.

title: Correlation identities omit their nonzero-variance domain

evidence.detail: rho is defined with sqrt(Var X) sqrt(Var Y) in the denominator, then subsequent rho identities are stated without requiring the relevant variances to be positive.

why: For a constant X or Y rho is undefined, while the text asserts rho in [-1,1] and formulas that divide by the same zero quantities.
suggested_correction: Attach 'when the stated variances are positive' to rho's definition, the |rho|=1 characterization, and the part-versus-whole formulas.

title: Lecture 14 has no learner exercise section despite introducing a multi-step applied method

evidence.detail: The lecture develops OLS coefficients, residual variance, and tests but contains no section titled 'Задачи' and no worked numerical fit.
The preceding inference lecture does provide a targeted exercise; lecture 14 ends after its formulas.

why: This leaves the new design condition, n-2 degrees of freedom, and use of t tables unpracticed; it also makes the condition omissions in CF-F01 harder to catch by application.
suggested_correction: Add at least one numerical OLS fit plus one inference exercise that requires checking A>0 and n>2.
